paragraphs.sourceText: Stunt people (替身演员) are not movie stars, but they are the hidden heroes of many movies. They were around long before films. Even Shakespeare may have used them in fight scenes. To be good, a fight scene has to look real. Punches must 26 enemies’ jaws. Sword fights must be fought with 27 swords. Several actors are usually in a fight scene. Their moves must be set up so that no one gets hurt. It is almost like planning a dance performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 替身演员不是电影明星，但他们是许多电影的隐藏英雄。他们早在电影出现之前就已经存在了。甚至莎士比亚也可能在打斗场面中使用过它们。要想表现出色，打斗场面必须看起来很真实。拳头必须打在敌人的下巴上。剑战必须使用锋利的剑。打斗场面通常由多名演员参与。他们的行动必须安排得当，以免有人受伤。这几乎就像计划一场舞蹈表演。

paragraphs.sourceText: If a movie scene is dangerous, stunt people usually 28 the stars. You may think you see Tom Cruise running along the top of a train. But it is 29 his stunt double. Stunt people must 30 the stars they stand in for. Their height and build should be about the same. But when close-ups are needed, the film 31 the star.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果电影场景很危险，通常会由特技演员来代替明星。您可能认为您看到汤姆·克鲁斯沿着火车顶部奔跑。但这可能是他的替身演员。特技演员必须与他们所代表的明星相似。他们的身高和体格应该大致相同。但当需要特写镜头时，影片就会聚焦于明星。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some stunt people 32 in certain kinds of scenes. For instance, a stunt woman named Jan Davis does all kinds of jumps. She has leapt from planes and even off the top of a waterfall. Each jump required careful planning and expert 33 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 有些特技演员专门从事某些特定的场景。例如，一位名叫简·戴维斯的特技演员会做各种跳跃动作。她曾从飞机上跳下，甚至从瀑布顶上跳下。每次跳跃都需要仔细的计划和专家的计时。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yakima Canutt was a famous cowboy stunt man. Among other stunts, he could jump from a second story window onto a horse’s back. He 34 the famous trick of sliding under a moving stagecoach. Canutt also 35 a new way to make a punch look real. He was the only stunt man ever to get an Oscar.
paragraphs.translationZh: 亚基马·坎纳特是一位著名的牛仔特技演员。除了其他特技之外，他还可以从二楼的窗户跳到马背上。他发明了在移动的驿马车下滑行的著名技巧。卡纳特还想出了一种让拳击看起来更真实的新方法。他是唯一一位获得奥斯卡奖的特技演员。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: As an Alaskan fisherman, Timothy June, 54, used to think that he was safe from industrial pollutants(污染物）at his home in Haines—a town with a population of 2,400 people and 4,000 eagles, with 8 million acres of protected wild land nearby. But in early 2007, June agreed to take part in a 36 of 35 Americans from seven states. It was a biomonitoring project, in which people’s blood and urine (尿) were tested for 37 of chemicals—in this case, three potentially dangerous classes of compounds found in common household 38 like face cream, tin cans, and shower curtains. The results— 39 in November in a report called “Is It in Us?” by an environmental group—were rather worrying. Every one of the participants, 40 from an Illinois state senator to a Massachusetts minister, tested positive for all three classes of pollutants. And while the 41 presence of these chemicals does not 42 indicate a health risk, the fact that typical Americans carry these chemicals at all 43 June and his fellow participants.

Clearly, there are chemicals in our bodies that don’t 44 there. A large, ongoing study conducted by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has found 148 chemicals in Americans of all ages. And in 2005, the Environmental Working Group found an 45 of 200 chemicals in the blood of 10 new-borns. “Our babies are being born pre-polluted,” says Sharyle Patton of Commonweal, which cosponsored “Is It in Us?” “This is going to be the next big environmental issue after climate change. ”

Directions：In this section, you are-going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. In Hard Economy for All Ages, Older Isn’t Better…It’s Brutal
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。在适合所有年龄段的硬经济中，年龄越大并不越好……这很残酷

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Young graduates are in debt, out of work and on their parents’ couches. People in their 30s and 40s can’t afford to buy homes or have children. Retirees are earning near-zero interest on their savings.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 年轻的毕业生负债累累，失业，躺在父母的沙发上。 30多岁和40多岁的人买不起房子，也买不起孩子。退休人员的储蓄利息几乎为零。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) In the current listless (缺乏活力的）economy, every generation has a claim to having been most injured. But the Labor Departments latest jobs reports and other recent data present a strong case for crowning baby boomers (二战后生育高峰期出生的人）as the greatest victims of the recession and its dreadful consequences.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 在当前缺乏活力的经济中，每一代人都声称自己受到了最严重的伤害。但劳工部最新的就业报告和其他最新数据有力地证明，婴儿潮一代是经济衰退及其可怕后果的最大受害者。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) These Americans in their 50s and early 60s—those near retirement age who do not yet have access to Medicare and Social Security—have lost the most earnings power of any age group, with their household incomes 10 percent below what they made when the recovery began three years ago, according to Sentier Research, a data analysis company. Their retirement savings and home values fell sharply at the worst possible time: just before they needed to cash out. They are supporting both aged parents and unemployed young-adult children, earning them the unlucky nickname “ Generation Squeeze. ’’
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 根据数据分析公司 Sentier Research 的数据，这些 50 多岁和 60 岁出头的美国人——那些接近退休年龄但尚未享受医疗保险和社会保障的人——在所有年龄段中失去了最大的收入能力，他们的家庭收入比三年前经济复苏开始时低了 10%。他们的退休储蓄和房屋价值在最糟糕的时候急剧下跌：就在他们需要兑现之前。他们既赡养年迈的父母，又赡养失业的年轻成年子女，这为他们赢得了“挤压一代”这个不吉利的绰号。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) New research suggests that they may die sooner, because their health, income security and mental well-being were ( 重创) by recession at a crucial time in their lives. A recent study by economists at Wellesley College found that people who lost their jobs in the few years before becoming qualified for Social Security lost up to three years from their life expectancy (预期寿命),largely because they no longer had access to affordable health care.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 新的研究表明，他们可能会死得更快，因为他们的健康、收入保障和心理健康在人生的关键时刻因经济衰退而受到重创。韦尔斯利学院经济学家最近的一项研究发现，在获得社会保障资格之前的几年内失业的人的预期寿命最多会缩短三年，这主要是因为他们无法再获得负担得起的医疗保健。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Unemployment rates for Americans nearing retirement are far lower than those for young people, who are recently out of school, with fewer skills and a shorter work history. But once out of a job, older workers have a much harder time finding another one. Over the last year, the average duration of unemployment for older people was 53 weeks, compared with 19 weeks for teenagers, according to the Labor Department’s jobs report released on Friday.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 接近退休的美国人的失业率远低于刚刚失学、技能较少、工作历史较短的年轻人。但一旦失业，年长的工人就很难找到另一份工作。根据劳工部周五发布的就业报告，去年，老年人的平均失业时间为 53 周，而青少年的平均失业时间为 19 周。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The lengthy process is partly because older workers are more likely to have been laid off from industries that are downsizing, like manufacturing. Compared with the rest of the population, older people are also more likely to own their own homes and be less mobile than renters, who can move to new job markets.
paragraphs.translationZh: F）这一漫长的过程部分是因为老年工人更有可能被制造业等裁员行业解雇。与其他人口相比，老年人也更有可能拥有自己的住房，并且比租房者流动性更小，租房者可以搬到新的就业市场。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Older workers are more likely to have a disability of some sort, perhaps limiting the range of jobs that offer realistic choices. They may also be less inclined, at least initially, to take jobs that pay far less than their old positions.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 老年工人更有可能患有某种残疾，这可能限制了提供现实选择的工作范围。他们也可能不太愿意接受薪酬远低于原来职位的工作，至少在最初是这样。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Displaced boomers also believe they are victims of age discrimination, because employers can easily find a young, energetic worker who will accept lower pay and who can potentially stick around for decades rather than a few years.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 流离失所的婴儿潮一代还认为他们是年龄歧视的受害者，因为雇主很容易找到年轻、精力充沛的工人，他们愿意接受较低的工资，并且有可能在公司工作几十年而不是几年。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) In a survey of older workers who were laid off during the recession, just one in six had found another job, and half of that group had accepted pay cuts. 14% of the re-employed said the pay in their new job was less than half what they earned in their previous job. “I just say to myself：‘ Why me? What have I done to deserve this?’ ’’ said John Agati，56，whose last full-time job, as a product developer, ended four years ago when his employer went out of business. That position paid $90,000, and his resume lists jobs at companies like American Express, Disney and USA Networks. Since being laid off, though, he has worked a series of part-time, low-wage, temporary positions, including selling shoes at Lord & Taylor and making sales calls for a car company.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 在一项针对经济衰退期间被解雇的老年工人的调查中，只有六分之一的人找到了另一份工作，其中一半人接受了减薪。 14%的再就业者表示，新工作的工资还不到上一份工作的一半。 56 岁的约翰·阿加蒂 (John Agati) 说：“我只是对自己说：‘为什么是我？我做了什么才配得到这样的待遇？’”他的最后一份全职工作是产品开发人员，四年前他的雇主倒闭了。他的这份工作年薪 9 万美元，他的简历列出了美国运通、迪士尼和美国电视网等公司的工作经历。不过，自从被解雇后，他从事过一系列兼职、低薪的临时职位，包括在 Lord & Taylor 和为一家汽车公司进行销售拜访。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) The last few years have taken a toll not only on his family’s finances, but also on his feelings of self- worth. “You just get sad,” Mr. Agati said. “I see people getting up in the morning, going out to their careers and going home. I just wish I was doing that. Some people don’t like their jobs, or they have problems with their jobs, but at least they’re working. I just wish I was in their shoes.” He said he cannot afford to go back to school, as many younger people without jobs have done. Even if he could afford it, economists say it is unclear whether older workers like him benefit much from more education.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 过去几年不仅对他的家庭经济状况造成了影响，也对他的自我价值感造成了影响。 “你只会感到悲伤，”阿加蒂先生说。 “我看到人们早上起床，出去工作然后回家。我只是希望我能这么做。有些人不喜欢他们的工作，或者他们的工作有问题，但至少他们在工作。我只是希望我能处于他们的处境。”他说，他无力像许多没有工作的年轻人那样重返学校。经济学家表示，即使他能负担得起，也不清楚像他这样的老年工人是否能从更多的教育中受益匪浅。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) “It just doesn’t make sense to offer retraining for people 55 and older,” said Daniel Hamermesh, an economics professor. “Discrimination by age, long-term unemployment, and the fact that they’ve now at the end of the hiring queue just don’t make it sensible to invest in them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 经济学教授 Daniel Hamermesh 表示：“为 55 岁及以上的人提供再培训是没有意义的。” “年龄歧视、长期失业，以及他们现在排在招聘队列末尾的事实，都不会让投资他们变得明智。”

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Many displaced older workers are taking this message to heart and leaving the labor force entirely. The share of older people applying for Social Security early rose quickly during the recession as people sought whatever income they could find. The penalty they will pay is permanent, as retirees who take benefits at age 62 will receive as much as 30% less in each months check for the rest of their lives than they would if they had waited until full retirement age (66 for those born after 1942).
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 许多失业的老年工人牢记这一信息并完全离开劳动力队伍。在经济衰退期间，随着人们寻求一切能找到的收入，提前申请社会保障的老年人比例迅速上升。他们将支付的罚款是永久性的，因为在 62 岁领取福利的退休人员在余生中每月领取的支票将比等到完全退休年龄（1942 年之后出生的人为 66 岁）少领取 30%。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Those not yet qualified for Social Security are increasingly applying for another, comparable kind of income support that often goes to people who expect never to work again：disability benefits. More than one in eight people in their late 50 s is now on some form of federal disability insurance program, according to Professor Mark Duggan at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 那些还没有资格获得社会保障的人越来越多地申请另一种类似的收入支持，这种收入支持通常提供给那些希望永远不再工作的人：残疾福利。宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院教授马克·杜根 (Mark Duggan) 表示，超过八分之一的 50 多岁的人现在正在参加某种形式的联邦残疾保险计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The very oldest Americans, of course, were battered by some of the same ill winds that tormented (折磨）those now nearing retirement, but at least the most senior were cushioned by a more readily available social safety net. More important, in a statistical twist, they may have actually benefited from the financial crisis in the most fundamental way: longer lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: N）当然，最年长的美国人也受到了一些与那些现在接近退休的人相同的恶风的打击，但至少最年长的人得到了更容易获得的社会安全网的缓冲。更重要的是，在统计上的扭曲，他们实际上可能以最根本的方式从金融危机中受益：更长的寿命。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Death rates for people over 65 have historically fallen during recessions, according to a November 2011 study by economists at the University of California, Davis. Why? The researchers argue that weak job markets push more workers into accepting relatively undesirable work at nursing homes, leading to better care for residents.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 根据加州大学戴维斯分校经济学家 2011 年 11 月的一项研究，历史上，65 岁以上人群的死亡率在经济衰退期间有所下降。为什么？研究人员认为，疲软的就业市场迫使更多的工人在疗养院接受相对不受欢迎的工作，从而为居民提供更好的护理。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Greater mobility puts younger people at an advantage in seeking new jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 更大的流动性使年轻人在寻找新工作时处于优势。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Many of the older workers laid off during the recession had to accept lower pay in their new jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 许多在经济衰退期间被解雇的老年工人不得不接受新工作中较低的工资。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Those who lose their jobs shortly before retirement age live a shorter-than-average life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 那些在退休年龄前不久失业的人的寿命短于平均水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Seniors at nursing homes could benefit from the weak job market.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 疗养院的老年人可以从疲软的就业市场中受益。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. Age discrimination in employment makes it pointless retraining older workers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 就业中的年龄歧视使得对老年工人进行再培训毫无意义。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. According to recent reports and data analyses, boomers suffer most from the weak economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 根据最近的报告和数据分析，婴儿潮一代受到经济疲软的影响最大。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Unemployed boomers are at a disadvantage in job-hunting because employers tend to hire younger workers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 失业的婴儿潮一代在找工作时处于不利地位，因为雇主倾向于雇用年轻工人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. People in their fifties and early sixties bear the heaviest family burdens.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 五十岁和六十岁出头的人承担着最重的家庭负担。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. People who take benefits from Social Security before official retirement age will get much less for the rest of their lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 在正式退休年龄之前领取社会保障福利的人在余生中获得的福利将少得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Older workers5 choice of jobs can be limited because of disability.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 老年工人5 由于残疾，工作选择可能受到限制。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: New Yorkers are gradually getting used to more pedaling (骑车的) passengers on those shining blue Citi Bikes. But what about local bike shops? Is Citi Bike rolling up riders at their expense?
paragraphs.translationZh: 纽约人逐渐习惯了更多骑车的乘客骑着闪亮的蓝色花旗自行车。但是当地的自行车商店呢？ Citi Bike 是否会以他们为代价吸引乘客？

paragraphs.sourceText: At Gotham Bikes in Tribeca, manager W. Ben said the shop has seen an increase in its overall sales due to the bike-share program. “ It’s getting more people on the road,’’ he said. James Ryan, an employee at Danny’s Cycles in Gramercy also said Citi Bike is a good option for people to ease into biking in a city famed for its traffic jams and aggressive drivers. “They can try out a bike without committing to buying one,” he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 翠贝卡的 Gotham Bikes 经理 W. Ben 表示，由于自行车共享计划，该店的整体销售额有所增加。他说：“这让更多的人上路。”格拉梅西 Danny’s Cycles 的员工詹姆斯·瑞安 (James Ryan) 也表示，对于人们在这座因交通拥堵和司机咄咄逼人而闻名的城市轻松骑自行车来说，Citi Bike 是一个不错的选择。“他们可以尝试一辆自行车，而无需承诺购买一辆，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rentals are not a big part of the business at either Gotham Bikes or Danny’s Cycles. But for Frank’s Bike Shop, a small business on Grand St. , the bike-share program has been bad news. Owner Frank Arroyo said his rental business has decreased by 90% since Citi Bike was rolled out last month. Arroyo’s main rental customers are European tourists, who have since been drawn away by Citi Bikes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无论是 Gotham Bikes 还是 Danny’s Cycles，租赁业务都不是其业务的重要组成部分。但对于格兰德街 (Grand St.) 的一家小企业弗兰克自行车店 (Frank’s Bike Shop) 来说，自行车共享计划却是个坏消息。业主 Frank Arroyo 表示，自从 Citi Bike 上个月推出以来，他的租赁业务减少了 90%。阿罗约的主要租赁客户是欧洲游客，此后他们被花旗自行车吸引走了。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, Ben said the bike-share is good for bike sales at his shop. People have used the bike- share and realized how great it is to bike in the city, then decide that they want something nicer for themselves,’’ he noted.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不过，本表示，共享单车有利于他店里的自行车销售。人们使用了共享单车，并意识到在城市骑自行车有多么棒，然后决定为自己提供更好的东西，”他指出。

paragraphs.sourceText: Christian Farrell of Waterfront Bicycle Shop, on West St. just north of Christopher St. , said initially he was concerned about bike-share, though, he admitted, “ I was happy to see people on bikes.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 位于克里斯托弗街以北西街的海滨自行车店的克里斯蒂安·法雷尔 (Christian Farrell) 表示，最初他对共享自行车感到担忧，但他承认，“我很高兴看到人们骑自行车。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Farrell’s early concerns were echoed by Andrew Crooks, owner of NYC Velo, at 64 Second Ave. “It seemed like a great idea, but one that would be difficult to implement,” Crooks said of Citi Bike. He said he worried about inexperienced riders’ lack of awareness of biking rules and strong negative reaction from non-cyclists. However, he said, ifs still too early to tell if his business has been impacted.
paragraphs.translationZh: 法雷尔早期的担忧得到了位于第二大道 64 号的纽约 Velo 老板安德鲁·克鲁克斯 (Andrew Crooks) 的呼应。“这似乎是一个好主意，但实施起来很困难，”克鲁克斯在谈到 Citi Bike 时说道。他说，他担心缺乏经验的骑手缺乏对骑车规则的认识，以及非骑车者的强烈负面反应。不过，他表示，现在判断他的业务是否受到影响还为时过早。

paragraphs.sourceText: While it’s possible bike-share will cause a drop in business, Crooks allowed that the idea is a positive step forward for New York City. 56 What is the author’s chief concern about the increasing use of Citi Bikes in New York?
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然共享单车可能会导致业务下降，但克鲁克斯承认，这个想法对纽约市来说是向前迈出的积极一步。 56 对于纽约花旗自行车的使用量不断增加，作者主要担心的是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 57 What happened to Gotham Bikes as a result of the bike-share program?
paragraphs.translationZh: 57 自行车共享计划给 Gotham Bikes 带来了什么影响？

paragraphs.translationZh: 59.为什么安德鲁·克鲁克斯认为共享单车计划很难执行？

paragraphs.translationZh: 60. 当地自行车商店对 Citi Bike 的总体态度如何？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Various studies have shown that increased spending on education has not led to measurable improvements in learning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 各种研究表明，教育支出的增加并没有带来学习方面的显着改善。

paragraphs.sourceText: Between 1980 and 2008, staff and teachers at US public schools grew roughly twice as fast as students. Yet students showed no additional learning in achievement tests.
paragraphs.translationZh: 1980 年至 2008 年间，美国公立学校教职员工的增长速度大约是学生的两倍。然而，学生们在成绩测试中没有表现出额外的学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: Universities show similar trends of increased administration personnel and costs without greater learning, as documented in Richard Arum and Josipa Roksa’s recent book Academically Adrift：Limited Learning on College Campuses.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正如理查德·阿鲁姆（Richard Arum）和约西帕·罗克萨（Josipa Roksa）最近出版的《学术漂泊：大学校园的有限学习》一书中所记录的那样，大学也表现出类似的趋势，即增加管理人员和成本，但没有更多的学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: A survey shows that 63% of employers say that recent college graduates don’t have the skills they need to succeed and 25% of employers say that entry-level writing skills are lacking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项调查显示，63% 的雇主表示应届大学毕业生不具备成功所需的技能，25% 的雇主表示缺乏入门级写作技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some simplistically attribute the decline in our public education system to the drain of skilled students by private schools, but far more significant events were at work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些人简单地将我们公共教育系统的衰落归因于私立学校流失高技能学生，但更重要的事件正在发生。

paragraphs.sourceText: Public schools worked well until about the 1970s. In fact, until that time, public schools provided far better education than private ones. It was the underperforming students who were thrown out of public schools and went to private ones.
paragraphs.translationZh: 直到 20 世纪 70 年代左右，公立学校都运转良好。事实上，在那之前，公立学校提供的教育远比私立学校好。那些表现不佳的学生被公立学校赶出并进入私立学校。

paragraphs.sourceText: A prominent reason public schools did well was that many highly qualified women had few options for working outside the house other than being teachers or nurses. They accepted relatively low pay, difficult working conditions, and gave their very best.
paragraphs.translationZh: 公立学校表现良好的一个重要原因是，许多高素质的女性除了当教师或护士之外几乎没有其他选择外出工作。他们接受相对较低的工资、艰苦的工作条件，并竭尽全力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Having such a large supply of talented women teachers meant that society could pay less for their services. Womens liberation opened up new professional opportunities for women, and, over time, some of the best left teaching as a career option, bringing about a gradual decline in the quality of schooling.
paragraphs.translationZh: 拥有如此大量有才华的女教师意味着社会可以为她们的服务支付更少的费用。妇女解放为妇女开辟了新的职业机会，随着时间的推移，一些最优秀的妇女离开了教学作为职业选择，导致学校教育质量逐渐下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: Also around that time, regulations, government, and unions came to dictate pay, prevent adjustments, and introduce bureaucratic (官僚的）standard for advancement. Large education bureaucracies and unions came to dominate the landscape, confusing activity with achievement. Bureaucrats regularly rewrite curriculums, talk nonsense about theories of education, and require ever more administrators. The end result has been that, after all the spending, students have worse math and reading skills than both their foreign peers and earlier generations spending far less on education— as all the accumulating evidence now documents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也是在那个时候，法规、政府和工会开始规定薪酬，阻止调整，并引入官僚主义的晋升标准。大型教育官僚机构和工会开始主导整个局面，混淆了活动与成就。官僚们经常重写课程，对教育理论胡说八道，并需要更多的管理人员。最终的结果是，在所有的支出之后，学生的数学和阅读技能比他们的外国同龄人和在教育上花费更少的前几代人要差——因为所有的教育支出都少得多。现在正在积累证据文件。

paragraphs.sourceText: 61. What do we learn from various studies on America’s public education?
paragraphs.translationZh: 61. 我们从有关美国公共教育的各种研究中学到了什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 62. How do some people explain the decline in public education?
paragraphs.translationZh: 62.有些人如何解释公共教育的衰落？

paragraphs.sourceText: 63. What was a significant contributor to the past glory of public schools?
paragraphs.translationZh: 63. 公立学校昔日辉煌的重要贡献者是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 64 Why did some of the best women teachers leave teaching?
paragraphs.translationZh: 64 为什么一些最优秀的女教师离开教学岗位？

paragraphs.sourceText: 65. What does the author think is one of the results of government involvement in education?
paragraphs.translationZh: 65.作者认为政府参与教育的结果之一是什么？
